 In The Court Of Mr. Vimal Kumar Yadav
 Food Safety Appellate Tribunal/
 Principal District & Sessions Judge,
 New Delhi District,
 Patiala House Courts, New Delhi 
Fsat No. 03/2023
Cnr No. Dlnd01-001814-2023
Raj Kumar Sharma, aged about 52 years
S/o Late Sh. Prabhu Ram Sharma

1A, Sewa Nagar Market, New Delhi-03. ... Appellant

 184-185, Shahjada Bagh,
 Phase-II, New Delhi-35. 
2. Inder Raj

 M/s. Krishna Masala Company,

 Appearances in Fsat No. 03/23 
Sh. Shiv Basoya, Ld. Counsel for appellant. 
Sh.Vinod Kumar Sharma, Ld. Chief Pp for the State/Respondent. 
Appearances in Fsat No. 01/23
Sh. M.L. Narang, Ld. Counsel for appellant. 
Sh.Vinod Kumar Sharma, Ld. Chief Pp for the State/Respondent. 
Sharwan Kumar vs State (F.S.O.) on 25 July, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/17337165/
1 Both the above referred appeals are taken up together being outcome of same order/adjudication. 
JUDGMENT 1. Aggrieved by the adjudication of the Adjudicating Officer/Additional District Magistrate instant appeals have been preferred, assailing the impugned order dated 11.01.2023 whereby the appellants were found to have violated the provisions of Section 26 (2) (ii) of Food Safety and Standard Act 2006 (the Act hereinafter) read with Section 3 (1) (zx) of the said Act which is punishable under Section 51 of the Act. The appellant was ordered to pay a penalty of Rs. 1 lac each (in case of Raj Kumar Sharma, FSAT No.03/2023) and Rs.50,000/- each (in case of Sharwan Kumar, FSAT No.01/2023). 
2. While assailing the order of the Adjudicating Officer, it is contended on behalf of Raj Kumar Sharma that he is not the manufacturer of the Dhaniya Powder, sample of which was bought on 11.12.2014 by the Food Safety Officer, from the shop of Raj Kumar Sharma of M/s. Shimla General Store, 1A, Sewa Nagar Market, New Delhi-03. The said Dhaniya Powder was in a sealed packet and four such sealed packets were taken. Those samples were further subjected to analysis and examination by the Food Safety Officer from NABL accredited FSAT No. 03/2023 & FSAT No.
01/2023 Page No.2 of 9 laboratory, where on examination it was found that sample was sub-standard since total ash on dry basis exceeded the prescribed maximum limit of 7.0% by weight. 
The Designated Officer was provided with the case file including the Food Analyst's report and Food Safety Officer's report, and after obtaining the sanction for prosecution under Section 36 (3) (e) of the Food Safety and Standards Act, 2006, an application was moved before the Adjudicating Officer for summoning, trial and punishment to the accused persons which ultimately resulted into the impugned order. 
3. There are two set of appellants, one is the grocery shop owner Raj Kumar Sharma, from whose shop M/s. Shimla General Store, sample of Dhaniya Powder in question was bought/lifted by the Food Safety Officer and the other is the manufacturer, which is a partnership firm having two partners. The stand of former is to the effect that he was selling a sealed and packed item manufactured by the other set of persons i.e. Krishna Masala Company, whereas latter has washed off its hands by asserting that the goods in question were not supplied by them and that they have no concern with this spurious/adulterated Dhaniya Powder, as no document, receipt, supply order etc. could be produced on record to connect them with sampled article. 
4. The Adjudicating Officer, who, in the impugned order held both set of persons i.e. Raj Kumar Sharma on one hand and Krishna Masala Company and its partners on the other hand responsible for the adulteration and after holding them FSAT No. 03/2023 & FSAT No. 01/2023 Page No.3 of 9 responsible, levied penalty of Rs. 1 lakh on Raj Kumar Sharma and Rs.50,000/- each on the partners of Krishna Masala Company.
5. It is contended on behalf of appellant Krishan Masala Company that there is no evidence on record which may reflect that item in question i.e. Dhaniya Powder was either manufactured or sold by them to Raj Kumar Sharma, FBO-cum- proprietor. In such circumstances, merely having address Sharwan Kumar vs State (F.S.O.) on 25 July, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/17337165/
2 on the label cannot be enough to link and connect the appellant Krishan Masala Company and its partners with the adulterated Dhaniya Powder. There is no investigation on this aspect and therefore, when the shop owner, who has failed to produce any document, which may have even remotely indicated that the "Dhaniya Powder" in question was supplied by Krishna Masala Company, then in these circumstances, the appellant Krishna Masala Company and its partners cannot be held responsible in any manner so far as, the instant matter is concerned. Ld. Counsel for appellant Krishna Masala Company has placed reliance on the judgment titled as M/s Parakh Food Limited Vs. State of AP [(2008 (1) (FAC 150)] and asserted that nobody can be prosecuted merely on the basis of label declaration of address of the manufactures. However, the observations in the judgment are in a different context and not about prosecuting the manufacturer on the basis of address alone. 
6. On the other hand, Ld. counsel for appellant Raj Kumar Sharma has sought to take advantage of Section 80 of the Act but in the absence of any document, which may connect the FSAT No.
03/2023 & FSAT No. 01/2023 Page No.4 of 9 product in question to the Appellant Krishna Masala Company, the arguments remain bald assertions, having no substance and therefore, appellant Raj Kumar Sharma cannot get any advantage. 
7. The circumstances emerging on record indicate that in the absence of any evidence connecting the product in question with the Krishna Masala Company, they cannot be held responsible. 
8. There is merely a declaration made by the accused/appellant Sh. Raj Kumar Sharma that he procured the Dhania powder from M/s. Krishna Masala Company but then, he could not produce any valid bill, invoice receipt or any such thing which may establish that product in question was procured from or was supplied by M/s. Krishna Masala Company. The details of M/s. Krishna Masala Company are there on the packet which prima facie indicate that the product was manufactured and supplied by M/s. Krishna Masala Company. However, in the absence of the bill,
invoice receipt, etc., this fact cannot be conclusively proved, especially when the appellant i.e. M/s.
Krishna Masala Company, through its partners, have taken a categorical stand that the product was not supplied by them. 
9. The investigation in this context is also not there inasmuch as if the Food Safety Officer (FSO)
wanted, he could have digged deep into it and various agencies and organizations like GST department and such other departments and could have ascertained the facts and to reach a conclusion about the supply or non-supply of Dhania powder by M/s. Krishna Masala FSAT No.
03/2023 & FSAT No. 01/2023 Page No.5 of 9 Company. This was not a difficult task. It is not a case of misbranding or label violations indicating that label containing all the details was there and intact. The packet bought as sample by the Food Safety Officer (FSO) had presumably all the details including the GST No./TIN No./batch No. of the product manufactured, etc on the product. There is practically no investigation on this aspect which was not that difficult as certain details have been obtained by the Food Safety Officer (FSO) from the VAT Officer in respect of M/s. Krishna Masala Company and in that eventuality, the other receipts and details available with M/s. Krishna Masala Company of the corresponding period when the sampled product was allegedly supplied to Food Safety Officer (FSO) then, it would have been clear as to whether M/s. Krishna Masala Company is Sharwan Kumar vs State (F.S.O.) on 25 July, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/17337165/
3 manufacturer or not, notwithstanding the fact that Raj Kumar Sharma was unable to furnish any bills, invoice of the bills, etc. In view of these facts, judgment relied upon by counsel for the appellant M/s. Krishna Masala Company come into play in case titled as Bhola Ram Vs. State of Punjab, Criminal Revision No. 1144 of 1984 decided on 31.01.1985, wherein in para No.3 it was observed in the following words :
"In the absence of a bill, cash memorandum or invoice in respect of the sale of any article of food given by a manufacturer or distributor or a dealer to a vendor, there could arise no presumption on the mere label or wrapper that the person purported to be the manufacturer distributor or dealer thereof is in fact such manufacturer,
distributor or dealer. The bare word of the vendor in that regard would not be enough. There had to be something more to it. On the file, there is no bill, cash memorandum or FSAT No. 03/2023 & FSAT No. 01/2023 Page No.6 of 9 invoice in respect of the article of food. Thus, no occasion for the present has arisen to employ even the provisions of Section 20-A of the Act in impleading the petitioner as an accused in the case. Thus in the circumstances, proceedings against the petitioner, on the present record, seem to be nothing but an abuse of the process of the Court. 
Proceedings against the petitioner are accordingly quashed, leaving it open to the learned Magistrate to proceed with the complaint in accordance with law. Nothing said herein would, however, prevent the Magistrate in summoning the petitioner at a later stage if evidence about his involvement is brought on the record. This petition is accordingly allowed with the aforesaid observations." 
10. Reference can also be made to Judgments in cases titled as Kishore Kumar Vs. State of Madhya Pradesh, [(2009) (2) FAC 333], R.K. Aggarwal vs. State of Haryana and Anr., Criminal Misc.
No.5943 of 1992 dated 29.10.1992 of the Punjab and Haryana High Court and Mohinder Kumar Vs.
State of Haryana, [(2004) (1) FAC 65].
It can thus be inferred that in the absence of bill, invoice or cash memo, mere details on the packet would not be sufficient to fasten the alleged manufacturer with a criminal liability. The courts have gone to the extent of holding that even summoning is improper in the absence of any memo, bill or receipt. The circumstances may reflect a strong suspicion against the appellant M/s. Krishna Masala Company which, due to lack of investigation by the Food Safety Officer (FSO), has been diluted. 
Therefore, in such circumstances the appellant, Krishna Masala Company, nevertheless, cannot be held responsible for the offence under which the Adjudicating Officer has held the FSAT No.
03/2023 & FSAT No. 01/2023 Page No.7 of 9 appellant M/s. Krishna Masala Company and its partners responsible and imposed a fine upon them. Evidently, the appellant Sharwan Kumar and Inder Raj, partners of M/s. Krishna Masala Company and the partnership firm cannot be held responsible for any offence. As a result, the appeal filed by the appellants (in case of Sharwan Kumar, FSAT No.01/2023) is allowed being maintainable. As such, the impugned order is set aside qua the present appellants. 
Sharwan Kumar vs State (F.S.O.) on 25 July, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/17337165/
4 11. Whereas, on the other hand, Raj Kumar Sharma is unable to show that the sealed item was procured by him from Krishna Masala Company and therefore, when he was the person who was found selling the same qua which there is no denial, therefore, he has been rightly held responsible by the Adjudicating Officer. Albeit the Adjudicating Officer has not tried to give reasons in his order,
which is by and large a non- speaking order indicating that he has taken the application along with documents filed before him to be the gospel truth and has not even attempted to obtain an affidavit from the Food Safety Officer, the witnesses arrayed by FSO to establish his case. However, in view of the admission made by appellant Raj Kumar Sharma, the sample was bought/lifted from his shop M/s. Shimla General Store, IA, Sewa Nagar Market, New Delhi-03 on 11.12.2014, there remains nothing much to be seen. 
12. Incidentally, the record of the Adjudicating Officer contains some judgments seemingly relied upon by the appellant M/s. Krishna Masala Company, but the Adjudicating Officer has not even cared to refer them in the impugned order, nor dealt FSAT No. 03/2023 & FSAT No. 01/2023 Page No.8 of 9 with them and passed the impugned order against the purported manufacturer. 
13. Considering the entire gamut of facts and circumstances, the appeal filed by the appellant Raj Kumar Sharma (in FSAT No.03/2023) is declined having no substance. Both the appeals stand disposed off accordingly.
14. The record of the Adjudicating Officer/Addl. District Magistrate, along-with copy of this judgment, be sent back. Both files of appeal be consigned to Record Room.

 Principal District & Sessions Judge  New Delhi District,
 Patiala House Courts, New Delhi.

summary.facts:
Aggrieved by the adjudication of the Adjudicating Officer/Additional District Magistrate instant appeals have been preferred, assailing the impugned order dated 11.01.2023 whereby the appellants were found to have violated the provisions of Section 26 (2) (ii) of Food Safety and Standard Act 2006 (the Act hereinafter) read with Section 3 (1) (zx) of the said Act which is punishable under Section 51 of the Act.
Those samples were further subjected to analysis and examination by the Food Safety Officer from NABL accredited FSAT No. 03/2023 & FSAT No.
01/2023 Page No.2 of 9 laboratory, where on examination it was found that sample was sub-standard since total ash on dry basis exceeded the prescribed maximum limit of 7.0% by weight.

The Designated Officer was provided with the case file including the Food Analyst's report and Food Safety Officer's report, and after obtaining the sanction for prosecution under Section 36 (3) (e) of the Food Safety and Standards Act, 2006, an application was moved before the Adjudicating Officer for summoning, trial and punishment to the accused persons which ultimately resulted into the impugned order.
summary.arguments:
In such circumstances, merely having address Sharwan Kumar vs State (F.S.O.) on 25 July, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/17337165/
2 on the label cannot be enough to link and connect the appellant Krishan Masala Company and its partners with the adulterated Dhaniya Powder.
There is no investigation on this aspect and therefore, when the shop owner, who has failed to produce any document, which may have even remotely indicated that the "Dhaniya Powder" in question was supplied by Krishna Masala Company, then in these circumstances, the appellant Krishna Masala Company and its partners cannot be held responsible in any manner so far as, the instant matter is concerned.
6. On the other hand, Ld. counsel for appellant Raj Kumar Sharma has sought to take advantage of Section 80 of the Act but in the absence of any document, which may connect the FSAT No.
03/2023 & FSAT No. 01/2023 Page No.4 of 9 product in question to the Appellant Krishna Masala Company, the arguments remain bald assertions, having no substance and therefore, appellant Raj Kumar Sharma cannot get any advantage.
summary.ANALYSIS:
8. There is merely a declaration made by the accused/appellant Sh. Raj Kumar Sharma that he procured the Dhania powder from M/s. Krishna Masala Company but then, he could not produce any valid bill, invoice receipt or any such thing which may establish that product in question was procured from or was supplied by M/s. Krishna Masala Company.
However, in the absence of the bill,
invoice receipt, etc., this fact cannot be conclusively proved, especially when the appellant i.e. M/s.
Krishna Masala Company, through its partners, have taken a categorical stand that the product was not supplied by them.
9. The investigation in this context is also not there inasmuch as if the Food Safety Officer (FSO)
wanted, he could have digged deep into it and various agencies and organizations like GST department and such other departments and could have ascertained the facts and to reach a conclusion about the supply or non-supply of Dhania powder by M/s. Krishna Masala FSAT No.
03/2023 & FSAT No. 01/2023 Page No.5 of 9 Company.
It is not a case of misbranding or label violations indicating that label containing all the details was there and intact.
The packet bought as sample by the Food Safety Officer (FSO) had presumably all the details including the GST No./TIN No./batch No. of the product manufactured, etc on the product.

10. Reference can also be made to Judgments in cases titled as Kishore Kumar Vs. State of Madhya Pradesh, [(2009) (2) FAC 333], R.K. Aggarwal vs. State of Haryana and Anr., Criminal Misc.
No.5943 of 1992 dated 29.10.1992 of the Punjab and Haryana High Court and Mohinder Kumar Vs.
State of Haryana, [(2004) (1) FAC 65].
It can thus be inferred that in the absence of bill, invoice or cash memo, mere details on the packet would not be sufficient to fasten the alleged manufacturer with a criminal liability.
The courts have gone to the extent of holding that even summoning is improper in the absence of any memo, bill or receipt.
The circumstances may reflect a strong suspicion against the appellant M/s. Krishna Masala Company which, due to lack of investigation by the Food Safety Officer (FSO), has been diluted.

Therefore, in such circumstances the appellant, Krishna Masala Company, nevertheless, cannot be held responsible for the offence under which the Adjudicating Officer has held the FSAT No.
03/2023 & FSAT No. 01/2023 Page No.7 of 9 appellant M/s. Krishna Masala Company and its partners responsible and imposed a fine upon them.
